# Election update: Sunday, November 8 (morning)

## Bottom line
No race was newly marked called overnight. The House results table stands at 418 of 435 races called: D 256, R 162, with 218 needed for a majority ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)). In the Senate, Democrats have secured 54 seats to Republicans' 44, counting seats not up, with 51 needed ([Senate table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). Alaska and Mississippi are still uncalled. FL-27 has officially gone to a recount ([Florida Politics](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiakFVX3lxTE1ncUVFOUhGUXplR1g0bXBSS05qclVyenA3MnRpbTRvcU1qanVPcDY5dkpSeHV4T1BwUHdJZ0htRGtuRjJTVGhqSDA3QldSM2YwamZobVdxRHg0TU1WQTM2c1o3VDJYWmJYdmc?oc=5)). No seat rated safe is within 5 points.

## Called since the last update
- No race was newly marked called in the results table, and no call was reversed.

## Legal and federal action
- **Florida:** the Miami Herald reports Rodriguez sued to remove Miami-Dade's election chief from the FL-27 recount ([Miami Herald](https://news.google.?oc=5)). A matching federal docket, Rodriguez v. Garcia (S.D. Fla., No. 1:26-cv-27895), shows a civil-rights complaint filed Nov. 6 and assigned to Judge Joan A. Lenard ([CourtListener](https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/75084109/rodriguez-v-garcia-et-al/)); the docket page could not be opened to confirm the parties.
- **California:** Reuters reports the administration ended its lawsuit over California ballots ([Reuters](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqwFBVV95cUxOMXMtNVM2c2ZyaGZ0ZTFLQUlLNjJyZUxWcFpJaVhEMmxwZDJNam1GdHBKWFVrT0syVGRiU25mZXlvbXRvNWlUbE95MVJYUHpSbFdYbm9HMEw1eS1KQVRTTjZpMmlzeDdHTjhPZlFDSFZhalJJdDFxd3VnRlNDVTFLY3JzV0N6WktFUVRITUMtS0dpQjB0Mlc2cnhwYm1SaERTcEtjZUVaZXpfYjQ?oc=5)); the court docket shows the Justice Department's notice of voluntary dismissal filed Nov. 6 ([CourtListener](https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/74967108/180/united-states-v-state-of-california/)).
- **Washington state:** a judge ruled federal officials cannot force Washington to set aside alleged noncitizen ballots, the Washington State Standard reports ([WA State Standard](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiugFBVV95cUxQRmEzZDV1RkdSVkdEQzREdjBtZ3JjSU5aR0xqRzNVMDd6RnEwQk5OeHo5OWdrUU9UTGJDUUwxOVBqQ2FwUi1NZjJSN05OallNWkZ0QktwQ0h0VUFMS0VTRWtFLXNtdVUwYnl2UEVrSkNOSmk3cjVmVW55VzVQalZKcmhpODh5ZEdCZWpUMWR4Y3JVYW0yQWZQTkdBLXRJSloxVVA5QmZlVFNKNWI1UXd4anFaaG9iVHRRMXc?oc=5)).
